jobOptions.title: Advanced options
jobOptions.writeModeHint: Upsert overwrites; insert skips existing keys; replace only updates existing ones.

info.writeMode: How each document is written. Upsert creates the document or overwrites one with the same key. Insert only creates new documents; keys that already exist are skipped and counted as skipped. Replace only updates documents that already exist; the rest are skipped.
info.batchSize: How many rows a reader fetches from PostgreSQL per round trip. Larger batches mean fewer round trips but more memory; the worker may use a smaller batch for wide rows to stay within its memory budget.
info.readParallelism: How many readers split one large table by primary-key range and read it at the same time, all from the same consistent snapshot. Each reader uses its own PostgreSQL connection. "auto" uses one reader per million rows, up to 8. Tables under 500,000 rows, or without a usable key, always use one reader.
info.writeConcurrency: The most documents being written to the target at the same time, for each table. The writer lowers this automatically when Couchbase is busy (timeouts, temporary failures) and raises it again when it recovers.
info.tableConcurrency: How many mappings (tables) migrate at the same time. Each one runs its own readers and writers, so higher values put more load on the source database, Couchbase and the worker. Tables start in order as slots free up.
info.maxDocsPerSecond: A speed limit for the whole job, to protect a cluster that also serves live traffic. Tables migrating in parallel share it, so the job never goes faster than this in total. Leave it empty for no limit.
info.durability: When Couchbase confirms each write. None: in memory on the active node (fastest; replicas catch up right after). Majority: in memory on a majority of replicas. Majority and persist on active: that, plus written to disk on the active node. Persist to majority: on disk on a majority of nodes (slowest, safest). Levels other than None need a bucket with replicas.
info.maxErrors: Rows that fail (a transform error, or a document the target rejects) are recorded on the Errors tab and the job carries on. The job stops as failed once this many rows have failed. 0 stops at the first failure; -1 never stops.
info.maxErrorRatio: The job also stops as failed when this share of the processed rows has failed, for example 0.01 = 1%. It is only checked after 10,000 rows, so a few early failures don't stop a job.
info.exactCount: Where the progress bar's total comes from. Auto counts rows exactly for tables up to 5 GB and uses PostgreSQL's estimate for bigger ones. Always counts every table exactly, which can take a while on very large tables. Never uses the estimate.
